```{python}
    plot_regions_per_lobe,
)
from pesco.io import load_sources, prepare_psd
from pesco.pipeline import DatasetCtx
from pesco.preprocess import compute_psd, normalize_psd
from pesco.spectral import afnan_band_overlap, remove_aperiodic, specparam2pandas

seed = 3
np.random.seed(seed)

PROJECT_DIR = Path("/Users/daniel/PhD/spectral-comparison/code/")
DATA_PATH_SOURCES = Path(f"{PROJECT_DIR}/data/Mantini2018")
DATA_PATH_IEEG = Path(f"{PROJECT_DIR}/data/Frauscher2018")

NO_PEAK_SUMMARY = "mean"
PLOT_SUMMARY = "median"

# specparam peak settings following Afnan et al. 2023, shared across every
# fit. aperiodic_mode is passed per fit: knee for iEEG, and both knee and
# fixed for HD-EEG so the two can be compared.
FREQ_RANGE = (0.5, 80.0)
R2_THRESHOLD = 0.9
SPECPARAM_SETTINGS = dict(
    peak_width_limits=[1, 8],
    max_n_peaks=8,
    peak_threshold=3.0,
)

fig_dir = Path("figures/chapter2")
fig_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

BANDS = [
    (0.5, 4.0, "δ"),
    (4.0, 8.0, "θ"),
    (8.0, 13.0, "α"),
    (13.0, 30.0, "β"),
    (30.0, 80.0, "γ"),
]


def metadata_columns(df):
    return [c for c in df.columns if isinstance(c, str)]


def relative_psd_df(psd_df, freqs):
    """Return PSD normalised to unit in-band power, preserving metadata."""
    freqs = np.asarray(freqs, dtype=float)
    rel = normalize_psd(psd_df[list(freqs)].to_numpy(dtype=float), freqs)
    return pd.DataFrame(rel, index=psd_df.index, columns=freqs).join(
        psd_df[metadata_columns(psd_df)]
    )


def peak_band(cf):
    if pd.isna(cf):
        return pd.NA
    for lo, hi, name in BANDS:
        if lo <= float(cf) < hi or (name == "γ" and float(cf) <= hi):
            return name
    return pd.NA


def peaks_with_metadata(fg, metadata_df, r2_threshold=R2_THRESHOLD):
    """Convert specparam peaks to a channel-level table with region labels."""
    peaks = specparam2pandas(fg)
    meta = (
        metadata_df[["Region name", "Lobe"]]
        .reset_index(drop=True)
        .reset_index(names="ID")
    )
    peaks = peaks.merge(meta, on="ID", how="left")
    peaks["fit_ok"] = peaks["gof_rsquared"] >= r2_threshold
    peaks["band"] = peaks["CF"].map(peak_band)
    return peaks


def peak_prevalence_by_region(peaks, band_order=("δ", "θ", "α", "β", "γ")):
    """Proportion of channels in each region with at least one peak per band."""
    channels = peaks.drop_duplicates("ID")
    if "fit_ok" in channels:
        channels = channels.loc[channels["fit_ok"]]
    denom = channels.groupby("Region name").size()
    present = (
        peaks.loc[peaks["fit_ok"] & peaks["CF"].notna()]
        .drop_duplicates(["ID", "Region name", "band"])
        .groupby(["Region name", "band"])
        .size()
        .unstack(fill_value=0)
    )
    prevalence = present.div(denom, axis=0).reindex(
        index=denom.index, columns=band_order, fill_value=0
    )
    prevalence = prevalence.fillna(0)
    return prevalence.sort_index()

ieeg_raw = DatasetCtx(name="intracranial data (raw)")
ieeg_raw.f, ieeg_raw.psd = prepare_psd(
    matfile =  DATA_PATH_IEEG / "WakefulnessMatlabFile.mat",
    region_dict_file = DATA_PATH_IEEG / "RegionInformation.csv",
    frauscher_bandpass = False,
    normalize=False,
)
assert ieeg_raw.psd is not None

ieeg_raw.psd
```


## Initial Afnan-style comparison: uncorrected spectra

The first comparison is deliberately run on the spectra *as measured*, before any explicit removal of the aperiodic component. This follows the first step of @afnan2023ValidatingMEGSource: the iEEG atlas is treated as the reference, the source-reconstructed HD-EEG as the estimated modality, and both are compared region by region in the shared MICCAI atlas. The only preprocessing applied here is the unit-power normalisation used by the Frauscher atlas, so the overlap reflects spectral shape rather than absolute signal amplitude. Thus, "uncorrected" means that the $1/f$ background remains in the spectra.

The initial analysis has three outputs. First, specparam is used only as a peak detector to list the periodic peaks present in the uncorrected iEEG spectra. Second, the same peak extraction is applied to the uncorrected HD-EEG source spectra. Third, the Afnan overlap metric is computed directly on the normalised PSDs, giving a baseline against which the later aperiodic-removed overlap can be compared.

```{python}
#| label: hd-load-raw
# HD-EEG source data: load_sources returns an mne.Raw + channel metadata
# (Region name, Lobe, ...). Compute the PSD from the time series.
sources_raw, sources_meta = load_sources(DATA_PATH_SOURCES)
hd_data = sources_raw.get_data()
hd_fs = sources_raw.info["sfreq"]
hd_f, hd_psd = compute_psd(hd_data, hd_fs, fmin=0.5, fmax=80.0)

hd_psd_df = pd.DataFrame(
    hd_psd, index=pd.Index(sources_raw.ch_names, name="ch_name"), columns=hd_f
).join(sources_meta)
hd_psd_df
```

```{python}
#| label: raw-relative-psd
# Afnan-style raw comparison: no aperiodic subtraction, but both modalities
# are converted to relative in-band power so unit differences do not dominate.
ieeg_rel = relative_psd_df(ieeg_raw.psd, ieeg_raw.f)
hd_rel = relative_psd_df(hd_psd_df, hd_f)
```

### Spectral overlap: uncorrected spectra

The Afnan overlap measure is then applied to the same uncorrected, relative-power PSDs. For each region and frequency bin, the median iEEG spectrum is compared with the median HD-EEG spectrum and scaled by the HD-EEG standard deviation. Values close to 1 indicate that the iEEG median lies close to the HD-EEG median; values of 0 indicate that the iEEG median falls outside one HD-EEG standard deviation. Averaging this quantity within canonical bands gives one raw-overlap score per region and band.

```{python}
#| label: afnan-overlap-raw
overlap_raw = afnan_band_overlap(
    ref_df=ieeg_rel, est_df=hd_rel,
    ref_freqs=ieeg_raw.f, est_freqs=hd_f,
)
overlap_raw
```

```{python}
#| label: afnan-overlap-raw-band-means
overlap_raw.mean().to_frame("mean overlap").T
```

```{python}

)
p.save(fig_dir / "afnan_overlap_raw_heatmap.pdf", width=6, height=10, dpi=300)
p.save(fig_dir / "afnan_overlap_raw_heatmap.svg", width=6, height=10, dpi=300)
p
```

## Oscillatory peak detection: after 1/f removal

The second comparison repeats the same logic after modelling and removing the aperiodic component. The aperiodic mode is chosen per modality based on prior literature. The iEEG atlas exhibits a visible knee in log-log space, motivating the knee model in line with reviews of intracranial 1/f activity [@donoghue2024EvaluatingComparingMeasures; @bush2024AperiodicComponentsLocal]. HD-EEG source-reconstructed spectra are typically near-linear in log-log space, where the fixed model is the standard choice [@donoghue2020ParameterizingNeuralPower]. Because the cross-modality comparison operates on the scale-free oscillatory residual $L_\text{osc} = \log_{10}(\text{PSD}/\text{PSD}_\text{ap})$ rather than on the aperiodic exponent itself, the modality-specific aperiodic mode is treated as a modelling choice to be checked in sensitivity analysis.

Intracranial and reconstructed sources from HD-EEG datasets themselves have different characteristics, so we used different settings for removing the 1/f background.
As orginally reported by @frauscher2018AtlasNormalIntracranial,the iEEG channel spectra exhibited a clear knee in log-log space, consistent with reports that knees are commonly observed in intracranial recordings. [@donoghue2024EvaluatingComparingMeasures; @bush2024AperiodicComponentsLocal]. We therefore  fit the iEEG spectra using Specparam's knee model. The HD-EEG  source-reconstructed spectra, by contrast, were approximately linear  in log-log space across the fitted frequency range and did not exhibit  a clear knee; we therefore used the fixed (no-knee) Specparam model  for these data, in line with standard practice for scalp/source M/EEG [@donoghue2020ParameterizingNeuralPower].

For each channel, the empirical PSD was parameterised over 0.5-80 Hz with peak_width_limits = [1, 8] Hz, max_n_peaks = 8, peak_threshold = 3.0 (in units of standard deviation of the residual), and aperiodic_mode = "knee".
In knee mode, the aperiodic component is modelled in log-power space as

$$L_\text{ap}(f) = b - \log_{10}\bigl(k + f^{\chi}\bigr),$$

where $b$ is the offset, $k$ the knee parameter, and $\chi$ the exponent governing the high-frequency roll-off. 
The fitted parameters $(b, k, \chi)$ were extracted per channel and used to reconstruct $L_\text{ap}(f)$ on the fitted frequency grid. The oscillatory residual was obtained by subtracting the aperiodic fit from the empirical log-PSD,


$$L_\text{osc}(f) = \log_{10} \text{PSD}(f) - L_\text{ap}(f),$$

which is the log-ratio of empirical power to the aperiodic component, equivalently $L_\text{osc}(f) = \log_{10}\bigl(\text{PSD}(f) / \text{PSD}_\text{ap}(f)\bigr)$. Values above zero indicate power exceeding the aperiodic fit; values below zero indicate power below it. This is the flattened spectrum in the sense of specparam.


The resulting $L_\text{osc}$ was carried forward to the clustering analysis without further normalisation, preserving the channel-relative scaling implied by the aperiodic subtraction.


<!-- Fit quality was assessed via the goodness-of-fit $R^2$ reported by specparam; across the iEEG channels, the median $R^2$ was 0.98, with 1765/1772 channels exceeding $R^2 \geq 0.9$.  -->

```{python}
#| label: ieeg-remove-aperiodic
# Afnan 2023-style 1/f removal: subtract the fitted aperiodic component
# in log10-power space. mode="log" -> L_osc = log10(PSD) - L_ap, the
# scale-free log-ratio residual (specparam flattened spectrum).
# mode="linear" available for IRASA-style normalised additive power.
osc_freqs, osc_mat = remove_aperiodic(fg, mode="log")

# Wrap as a DataFrame with the same channel index and metadata as ieeg_raw.psd.
# fg was fit on rows of ieeg_raw.psd in order, so rows align by position.
meta_cols = [c for c in ieeg_raw.psd.columns if isinstance(c, str)]
ieeg_osc = pd.DataFrame(
    osc_mat, index=ieeg_raw.psd.index, columns=osc_freqs
).join(ieeg_raw.psd[meta_cols])
ieeg_osc
```

## HD EEG Data 

For the HD-EEG source data we applied the same aperiodic removal as for the iEEG atlas. To keep the recovered oscillatory residuals directly comparable between the two modalities, the specparam settings followed @afnan2023ValidatingMEGSource and were identical across datasets: fitting range 0.5-80 Hz, peak width limits 1-8 Hz, a maximum of 8 peaks, and a peak threshold of 3.0 SD. The aperiodic component was subtracted in log-power space and the resulting log-ratio residual $L_\text{osc}$ retained, exactly as for the iEEG atlas above.

The aperiodic mode is the one setting that cannot be transferred uncritically between modalities. @frauscher2018AtlasNormalIntracranial report a clear spectral knee in intracranial recordings, which motivates the knee model $L_\text{ap}(f) = b - \log_{10}(k + f^{\chi})$ for the iEEG atlas. Source-reconstructed HD-EEG spectra, by contrast, are frequently close to linear in log-log space across the fitted range, where the fixed model $L_\text{ap}(f) = b - \chi\log_{10}(f)$ is the more common choice [@donoghue2020ParameterizingNeuralPower]. Because the exponents returned by the two modes are not on the same scale, we do not compare them directly. Instead, we fit the HD-EEG spectra in **both** knee and fixed mode and quantify the consequence of the choice: for each channel we compute the Pearson correlation between the knee- and fixed-mode oscillatory residuals. A correlation close to one indicates that the mode choice has little effect on the recovered oscillations, so either model may be used; a low correlation would flag the aperiodic mode as a confound for the cross-modality comparison.

```{python}
#| label: hd-load
# HD-EEG PSD was loaded above for the uncorrected comparison and is reused
# here so the aperiodic-removal analysis starts from the same spectra.
hd_psd_df
```

```{python}
#| label: hd-fit
# Fit specparam in both knee and fixed aperiodic mode, same Afnan settings
# as iEEG. Source HD-EEG spectra are often near-linear in log-log space, so
# fitting both lets us quantify how much the mode choice changes the result.
hd_freqs = np.asarray(hd_f, dtype=float)
hd_psd_mat = hd_psd_df.iloc[:, : len(hd_freqs)].to_numpy(dtype=float)

fg_hd_knee = SpectralGroupModel(**SPECPARAM_SETTINGS, aperiodic_mode="knee")
fg_hd_knee.fit(hd_freqs, hd_psd_mat, freq_range=list(FREQ_RANGE), n_jobs=1)

fg_hd_fixed = SpectralGroupModel(**SPECPARAM_SETTINGS, aperiodic_mode="fixed")
fg_hd_fixed.fit(hd_freqs, hd_psd_mat, freq_range=list(FREQ_RANGE), n_jobs=1)

fg_hd_knee.report()
fg_hd_fixed.report()
```

```{python}

_, osc_hd_fixed = remove_aperiodic(fg_hd_fixed, mode="linear")

meta_cols_hd = [c for c in hd_psd_df.columns if isinstance(c, str)]
hd_osc_knee = pd.DataFrame(
    osc_hd_knee, index=hd_psd_df.index, columns=osc_freqs_hd
).join(hd_psd_df[meta_cols_hd])
hd_osc_fixed = pd.DataFrame(
    osc_hd_fixed, index=hd_psd_df.index, columns=osc_freqs_hd
).join(hd_psd_df[meta_cols_hd])
hd_osc_knee
```

```{python}

# oscillatory residuals. r near 1 => the aperiodic-mode choice barely

r_knee_fixed = pd.Series(
    [np.corrcoef(osc_hd_knee[i], osc_hd_fixed[i])[0, 1]
     for i in range(len(osc_hd_knee))],
```

For each region in each dataset, the primary aperiodic parameters of interest were the exponent ($\chi$) and offset ($b$). Oscillatory peaks were characterised by their centre frequency, power, and bandwidth. Model fits were evaluated using $R^2$ and mean absolute error; fits with $R^2$ below 0.90 were flagged for inspection.

### Comparing the oscillatory distributions

The aperiodic-removed spectra ($L_\text{osc}$) of the two modalities are compared at two levels.

As an *exploratory* step, the per-channel residual spectra within each dataset are clustered into a small number of spectral types, separating channels dominated by a single rhythm from those with no clear oscillatory peak. This clustering is purely descriptive: it summarises the range of oscillatory profiles present in each modality. The clusters are, however, estimated separately for each dataset and their identities are not shared across modalities, so comparing cluster solutions between iEEG and HD-EEG directly would confound genuine spectral differences with the instability of the clustering. The clustering is therefore not used to support the cross-modality claim.

The *confirmatory* comparison instead follows @afnan2023ValidatingMEGSource and operates directly on the spectra, with no intervening clustering step. Because $L_\text{osc}$ is scale-free, this comparison remains valid despite the differing physical units of intracranial potentials and reconstructed source activity.

Channels are first pooled across hemispheres: the iEEG atlas and the source montage both label channels with a hemisphere-agnostic region name, so grouping by that label collapses the left/right ROIs into the 38 bilateral regions of the MICCAI atlas, exactly as in @afnan2023ValidatingMEGSource. Within each region $r$, the iEEG atlas is taken as the reference modality and the HD-EEG source data as the estimated modality. Let $\widetilde{L}_r(f)$ denote the median of $L_\text{osc}$ across the channels of region $r$ at frequency bin $f$, and $\text{SD}^{\,\text{HD}}_r(f)$ the corresponding standard deviation in the HD-EEG modality. The bin-wise overlap is

$$\text{overlap}_r(f) = \begin{cases} 1 - \dfrac{\bigl\lvert \widetilde{L}^{\,\text{iEEG}}_r(f) - \widetilde{L}^{\,\text{HD}}_r(f)\bigr\rvert}{\text{SD}^{\,\text{HD}}_r(f)}, & \bigl\lvert \widetilde{L}^{\,\text{iEEG}}_r(f) - \widetilde{L}^{\,\text{HD}}_r(f)\bigr\rvert \le \text{SD}^{\,\text{HD}}_r(f) \\[3mm] 0, & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases}$$

The metric equals 1 when the iEEG median lands exactly on the HD-EEG median and decreases linearly to 0 once the two medians differ by one HD-EEG standard deviation, so it measures whether the reference spectrum falls within the spread of the estimated modality. The overlap is averaged across the frequency bins of each canonical band ($\delta$ 0.5-4, $\theta$ 4-8, $\alpha$ 8-13, $\beta$ 13-30, $\gamma$ 30-80 Hz), yielding one value per region per band. The aperiodic mode used for the HD-EEG fit is the knee model; the fixed-mode residual can be substituted to confirm that the comparison is insensitive to that choice (see the knee-vs-fixed correlation above).

```{python}
#| label: afnan-overlap
# Afnan 2023 average overlap: iEEG (reference) vs HD-EEG (estimated),
# per region per band, on the aperiodic-removed residual L_osc.
# Channels are pooled across hemispheres by grouping on "Region name".
overlap_knee = afnan_band_overlap(
    ref_df=ieeg_osc, est_df=hd_osc_knee,
    ref_freqs=osc_freqs, est_freqs=osc_freqs_hd,
)
overlap_knee
```

```{python}
#| label: afnan-overlap-band-means
# Mean overlap per band across all regions (Afnan-style summary).
overlap_knee.mean().to_frame("mean overlap").T
```

```{python}
p = plot_overlap_heatmap(
    overlap_knee, title="iEEG vs HD-EEG overlap (knee, $L_{osc}$)"
)
p.save(fig_dir / "afnan_overlap_heatmap.svg", width=6, height=10, dpi=300)
p
```
